question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+4}{3},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩=39.
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(3,1,-4)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨5,2,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨3,1,-4⟩+t⟨5,2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ ⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ (-3)(3+5t)+2(1+2t)-(-4+3t) & =39 \\ -9-15t+2+4t+4-3t & =39 \\ -14t & =42 \\ t & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-3$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-3),1+2(-3),-4+3(-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-12,-5,-13⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(-12,-5,-13).$
